description.en:
"Does the big guy's ghost really not come back at all? It's been so long, I kind of miss her."
"That person has a lot on her plate in Lungmen, after all."
"Moumouxiang went out of town again recently. It was always quite interesting listening to her talk about the ins and outs of the showbiz... You better stay a few days longer this time back, or I'll die of boredom."
"Didn't Your Divinity say you wanted to visit the North Courtyard?"
"Hmph, we'll see. Oh, right, a young man came to the shrine every day to draw fortunes a few days ago. But even though the lazy ghost was squatting right at his feet, he just kept staring at his terminal, and in the end, he complained that the shrine's deity wasn't efficacious."
"Heh, that deity of ours sure gets wronged. Alright, here are the rice balls packed by you and the Head Priestess. Have a safe trip, sir."
Moriuchi Toru absentmindedly inserted the occult video tape he happened to purchase a few days ago into the player, thinking of the conversation with the deity before closing shop, and how someone seemed to be filming in the direction the deity left after parting ways. The ghost story of the Wanyudo remains enduring, Moriuchi thought. The television screen, occasionally flashing with static, played blurry footage, as if the farce from a few months ago hadn't brought much impact here, and everyone was still tirelessly discussing new anecdotes.
People always seem to need things like this. After all, so-called ghost stories are nothing more than another form of gossip. At the very least, they can make a few people temporarily feel like they've encountered something a little out of the ordinary on some boring night. Encounters are probably much the same. Both Hoshiguma and Moumouxiang have left this place, and Kishisei has his own things to do. Although Sarasa's postcards still arrive occasionally, everyone hasn't gathered together in a long time. Moriuchi understood that people meeting and then parting ways of their own accord was never really a big deal to begin with.
The television screen suddenly flickered, and after another burst of static noise, Moriuchi saw himself. In the footage, he was waving at an empty unicycle and two cups of oden suspended in mid-air. Moriuchi couldn't help but feel a little amused. The deity he pursued for a lifetime was hard to see, while the deity he met by chance constantly appeared by his side, chattering about the situations of his companions. Yet in the eyes of the worldly, he had always been talking to thin air.
Moriuchi suddenly derived a strange sense of stability from this. Turns out, within those tiny sentiments he repeatedly picked up and used to comfort himself to keep moving forward, he too had once been gently gathered by someone into a certain piece of experience. Perhaps this stability still couldn't count as any definite hope, but since someone was willing to stop at his stall, listen to him say a few words of gossip, take away a few skewers of simmered food, and then treat this night as a ghost story to tell others, then Moriuchi thought, tentatively believing in it wouldn't be so bad either.
description.zh:
“大个子的鬼完全不回来吗？好久没见了，我还有点想她呢。”
“那位在龙门也有很多事要忙嘛。”
“萌萌香最近又去外地了，本来听她讲演艺圈的大小事还挺有趣的……你这一趟回来可得多待几天，不然我要无聊死了。”
“神明大人不是说想去北院看看？”
“哼，再说吧。对了，前几天有个年轻人每天都来神社求签，不过，懒鬼明明已经蹲在他脚边了，他却一直盯着终端看，最后还抱怨御机的神明不灵。”
“呵，那位神明大人可真是受委屈了。好了，您和宫司大人打包的竹轮。您慢走。”
森内彻漫不经心地将前些天自己偶然购入的怪谈录像带放入播放器，想到收摊前与神明的对话，以及告别之后，路边似乎有人正对着神明离去的方向拍摄。轮入道的怪谈倒是经久不衰，森内彻不由地想。偶尔闪过雪花点的电视屏幕里播放着模糊的影像，好似几个月前的那场闹剧并没有给这里带来多大的影响，大家依旧乐此不疲地谈论着新的逸闻。
人们似乎总是需要这样的东西。说到底，所谓怪谈，不过是另一种闲话，它们至少还能在某个无聊的夜里，让几个人暂时觉得自己碰见了一点不同寻常的东西。相遇大概也是这样。星熊和萌萌香都离开了这里，吉星也有自己要做的事，虽然更纱的明信片偶尔还会寄来，但大家已经很久没有聚在一起了。森内彻明白，人们相遇，再各自离开，本来就算不得什么大事。
电视屏幕忽然闪烁，又一阵雪花噪点后，森内彻看到了自己。画面中自己正对着空荡荡的独轮车和两杯悬在空中的关东煮挥手。森内彻不禁感到有些好笑，追寻了一生的神明难以得见，萍水相逢的神明反倒时常出现在自己身边，絮叨着伙伴们的境况。而在世人眼中，他一直在与空气对话。
森内彻突然从中得到一种奇异的安定。原来在那些他反复拾起，用来哄骗自己继续向前的微小情谊里，他也曾被谁这样轻轻地收进某段见闻之中。也许这份安定依旧算不上什么确切的希望，可既然有人愿意停在他的摊前，听他说几句闲话，带走几串煮物，再把这一晚当作怪谈讲给别人，那么森内彻想，暂且相信它也没什么不好。
